thread:
emma.r: heads-up — just got a high-priority support escalation from Acme: p99 for text-gen routes spiked from ~450ms to ~2.2s after this morning's rollout. noticed ~09:12 UTC. chart: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc123/view?orgId=1 :alarm_clock:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished at 08:58 UTC by mike.t (version runtime-1.22.0-mux) :white_check_mark:

mike.t: confirmed I pushed the multiplexing proxy swap to canary. it's the only change touching connection muxing + tenant demuxing. rolling 5 canary VMs, traffic split 10%.

sudha.k: pulling logs for tenant acme-42 now. seeing bursts of synchronous token refresh calls and transient 502/429 from auth-service. sample logs: ```2024-05-07T09:11:40Z proxy[mux]: reauth start tenant=acme-42 trace=tx123 status=200 uid=...``` then many requests wait on reauth loop.

olivia.oncall: running quick repro with curl to canary host (10.1.4.22): ```ab -n1000 -c20 http://10.1.4.22/v1/generate -p payload.json``` seeing long tail on requests that trigger token refresh.

mike.t: that matches suspicion: mux now multiplexes connections and serializes a refresh per-tenant slot; if token refresh is synchronous on the hotpath, it becomes head-of-line for other requests. i didn't expect auth to be a blocking call.

emma.r: immediate mitigations? customer is unhappy and latencies affect SLAs.

mike.t: i rolled back the mux binary on canary hosts 2/5 to previous runtime-1.21.9. will roll further if p99 improves. also bumping per-tenant conn limit to 200 as a short term.

sudha.k: created filtered log stream for acme-42 and added sampling to trace reauth durations. also opened a ticket for auth-service to add async refresh and jittered TTL.

support-bot: Incident INC-2024-135 created and customer notified (seq updated). sla: P1.

olivia.oncall: after rollback on 2 hosts, canary p99 for acme-42 dropped to ~520ms (was 2.2s) — still above baseline but trending down.

mike.t: rolling rollback to remaining canary hosts now, then will roll forward with a patch that makes token refresh async and moves it off the hotpath. planning a hotpatch to mux to short-circuit when token refresh is inflight.

emma.r: can you add a route-slew so acme-42 traffic goes to their dedicated pool while we stabilize? need minimal customer impact.

mike.t: done — routed acme-42 to dedicated pool + removed from canary split. monitoring.

sudha.k: collecting heap/latency flamegraphs and KV cache metrics. preliminary note: KV cache TTL for token entries was 0 on miss which forced immediate sync fetch. will add TTL + jitter and change miss-path to async refresh.

olivia.oncall: support updated customer with workaround and ETA ~3h for full rollback/hotpatch.

mike.t: hotpatch deployed to canary as v1.22.0-mux-hotfix: short-circuits token refresh and returns 401 with async refresh kick-off so clients can retry non-blocking. Observability flags enabled.

olive: typo: olivia.oncall: monitoring shows p99 fell to ~480ms after full rollback + route-slew + hotpatch. marking incident stabilized.

emma.r: next steps: open a postmortem, include repro steps, graphs, exact commit that introduced the mux change, and change request to make auth refresh async by default. add runbook note: avoid synchronous auth calls on multiplexing proxies.

mike.t: will follow up with PRs: (1) fix token refresh async + TTL+ jitter; (2) add per-tenant queue length guard and backpressure; (3) add canary traffic safety check to block mux swaps if auth hotpath not validated.

sudha.k: will attach logs/traces and a small synthetic repro harness to the postmortem.

emma.r: thanks everyone. customer is now back to baseline SLA, keeping monitoring for 6 hours, will file the postmortem by EOD. :thumbsup:
